single_points.text: One reviewer says the Paradox Launcher is comparable to malware and initially prevented them from playing the game while leaving junk folders in AppData.

citation.review_text:
The Paradox Launcher is comparable to malware and initially prevented me from even playing the game itself as well as left a bunch of junk folders in my computer's AppData.

If you're facing similar issues then proceed to try to input the following line into the Steam Properties > Launch Options for this game after uninstalling the Paradox Launcher from your computer:

"C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Cities_Skylines\Cities.exe" %command%

Hopefully this helps.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the base game feels barebones or incomplete, relying on paid downloadable content or mods to provide sufficient content and features.

citations.review_text: Cities: Skylines eventually stops feeling like a city builder and starts feeling like a traffic management simulator. The AI makes questionable decisions, performance falls apart as your city grows, and mods become almost essential to fix basic gameplay issues. On top of that, the base game feels incomplete without countless DLCs. For a game with this much potential, it's disappointing how heavily it relies on the player's patience and the community's work to deliver a decent experience.

This game is a barebone.

you can realize that about 2-3 hours in.

to give some flesh to the game, and to feel like you run a city and have many options, DLC's are required.
Many DLC's should have just been free updates, and can end up costing x5 than the full game depending on the bundle.

Base game has a good foundation but very little content. After just a few hours it seems like there is nothing left to do but make your city bigger. There aren't any long term goalposts. It's worth noting that I haven't tried out any mods for the game. But if it needs paid dlc or mods to make it interesting there's an issue.

claims.claim: The game requires mods to fix vanilla traffic management and supply missing quality of life features.

citations.review_text: Vanilla traffic management is impossible, but get yourself some mod and this game gets brilliant. Highly recommend either way!

This game is super fun, but before you buy, a couple of recommendations.

1. Buy this over the sequel. You'll save money and realize that the first game is miles better.

2. Prepare to spend money on DLCs. You'll realize that the DLCs are basically parts of the game that should've been features in the base. I recommend starting with Industries and Mass Transit, and if you are feeling crazy, get Campus, Parklife, and After Dark. There are some other really cool DLCs, so don't be afraid to do some research.

3. Get mods. The Cities: Skylines workshop has so many mods that basically remove the parts of the game that are a pain in the ass. You will realize that without mods, the base game is lacking a lot of important quality of life features. I recommend getting MoveIt!, TM:PE, 81 Tiles, and a couple other basic mods that will elevate your gameplay.

Overall, I really love this game, and its a shame how greedy the company is. Cities 2 could have been generational, but at the end of the day, the OG is the better pick. Get ready to be broke!

For the most part this game works fantastic in regards to a City builder. What annoys me is how we have to fully mod this game for it to do what it needs to be a fantastic and funtrional city. The second is just as bad if not worse.  The king of the genre with many many broken mods and mods that dont work with others to the point they break the game. That being said, when you get the right combination its amazing

citations.review_text: Paradox is effectively a dead gaming company just milking what money it can from it's assets. Shameful developers releasing half-finished sequels and then pushing out countless paid DLC titles for years without ever bothering to fix the base game (of the sequel and the original). I'll never buy another Paradox product again.

It was a good time, however they are trying to squeeze more DLC money out of it. It is 11 years old and has a successor, they shouldn't be trying to sell new DLC for it. The worst part is, I expect this to break mods that won't be updated.

the DLC for this version costs more than Cities Skylines 2, i don't recommend buying their games at full price, and i don't endorse companies having extortion-level prices on their DLC on a game now considered classic.

The game itself is great, I have over 650 hours played and regret nothing, though it is a huge downer that I can't play the game with all it's separate DLC pack because the creators rather line their pocket than simply provide a great game, instead hidden behind a paywall.  I already bought the game, DLC's should be included as they don't contain much content, just a theme with a price.  I've enjoyed the game for years and one day hope i can enjoy the game with all it's intended content, especially knowing it'd be cheaper at the moment to just buy Cities Skylines 2, but still forced to buy DLC's if i want the full game.

So, at this time, I'm not giving the creators another penny.

Boy, I never thought I'd be so chuffed to micromanage interchanges. The number of DLCs is definitely outrageous, but by the time you might care about them, you're already in deep enough to barely notice the extra bucks... but also, lots of things released in DLCs have correlates/replacements in the workshop.
It is fun. Buy the bikes. Extremely expensive with all the DLC. Probably still better than Cities 2

I love this game but Paradox are turning it into the Sims 4. Hundreds of dollars worth of DLC that barely add anything in some cases, or in worse cases add things that should have been base game content. 

They still haven't fixed core gameplay issues, just like SIms 4. All they do is just keep releasing DLC.
